# Use Case: View Veterinarians

## Overview

**Use Case ID:** UC-002   
**Use Case Name:** View Veterinarians   
**Primary Actor:** Visitor   
**Goal:** Browse the list of veterinarians employed at the clinic along with their specialties.   
**Status:** Approved   
**Requirements:** [FR-003, NFR-001, NFR-002, NFR-003, C-010, C-011](../requirements.md)

## Preconditions

- At least one veterinarian is recorded in the system (see A1 otherwise).

## Main Success Scenario

1. Visitor clicks the "Veterinarians" link in the navigation bar.
2. System retrieves the first set of veterinarians.
3. System renders the veterinarians grid showing, for each vet, the first name, last name, and a comma-separated list of
   specialties (or "none" if no specialties are held).
4. As the Visitor scrolls toward the end of the grid, the system fetches and appends the next chunk of veterinarians
   until all entries have been loaded.

## Alternative Flows

### A1: No Veterinarians Registered

**Trigger:** The clinic has no veterinarians recorded (step 2).
**Flow:**

1. System renders the veterinarians grid with no rows.
2. Use case ends.

## Postconditions

### Success Postconditions

- The veterinarians grid is rendered with all loaded entries.
- No data is modified.

### Failure Postconditions

- On data-access errors, the application error view is shown and no vet list is displayed.

## Business Rules

### BR-001: Lazy Loading

Realizes [GR-002: Lazy Loading of Lists](../business_rules.md#gr-002-lazy-loading-of-lists).

The list in question is the veterinarians grid.

### BR-002: Specialty Ordering

Realizes [GR-003: Deterministic Ordering](../business_rules.md#gr-003-deterministic-ordering).

The order in question is a vet's specialties, alphabetically by name.

### BR-003: Anonymous Access

Realizes [GR-001: Anonymous Access](../business_rules.md#gr-001-anonymous-access).

# Business Rules

Rules that more than one use case must honour.

A rule that belongs to a single use case stays **in** that use case as
`BR-NNN` — it is part of that use case's story and has no life of its own. A
rule that several use cases share lives **here** as `GR-NNN`, is stated once,
and is referenced by each use case that applies it. The use case keeps its local
`BR-NNN` heading, so tests and the traceability sensors still point at a rule of
that use case; the heading says which shared rule it realizes instead of
restating it.

`BusinessRuleTraceabilityTest` (`./mvnw test`) keeps the two sides honest: it
fails when a use case references a rule that does not exist, when a link lands
on a renamed heading, when the `**Realized by:**` line and the use cases
disagree in either direction, when the summary table drifts from the rules below
it, or when a rule here is realized by fewer than two use cases.

**Why `GR` and not `BR`.** `BR-NNN` ids are scoped to a use case: every
`UC-NNN-*.md` numbers its rules from `BR-001`, and `@UseCase(businessRules =

stand beside ten local ones and mean nothing on its own. `GR` — global rule —
is a second namespace precisely so that an id never needs a use case to

# Testing

Read this **before writing or modifying any test** under `src/test/java/`.

## Two test layers — the class suffix picks the Maven phase

| Layer                 | Suffix  | Runs in         | Framework                                              | Skill                               |
|-----------------------|---------|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Server-side view test | `*Test` | `./mvnw test`   | Vaadin Browserless (`SpringBrowserlessTest`)           | `aiup-vaadin-jooq:browserless-test` |
| Browser test          | `*IT`   | `./mvnw verify` | Playwright + Drama Finder (`AbstractBasePlaywrightIT`) | `aiup-vaadin-jooq:playwright-test`  |

Surefire picks up `*Test`, Failsafe picks up `*IT` (both configured via `spring-boot-starter-parent`; the failsafe
plugin is declared in `pom.xml`). A browserless test named `*IT` or a Playwright test named `*Test` runs in the wrong
phase, and `TestLayerConventionsTest` fails the build when one does. The rule is worth enforcing because the
failure is otherwise silent: nothing errors, the wrong Maven plugin simply never picks the class up, and a test
that never runs reports as passing. Browserless is the default for use cases; Playwright is for test cases (`TC-*`) and
anything that genuinely needs a browser (client-side rendering, keyboard focus, scrolling).

## Framework

- **Vaadin Browserless Testing** (`browserless-test-junit6` + `browserless-test-spring`) is the default for Vaadin view
  tests — server-side, no
  browser, no servlet container.
  Reference: https://vaadin.com/docs/latest/flow/testing/browserless/getting-started
- View tests extend `PetClinicTestBase` (or `SpringBrowserlessTest` directly for tests that don't touch the DB, in
  which case add `@SpringBootTest` and `@Import(TestcontainersConfiguration.class)` yourself).
  They run inside a Spring context and use the same Testcontainers Postgres as the rest of the tests.
- **Use the `aiup-vaadin-jooq:browserless-test` skill** to scaffold a browserless test for a use case. Prefer it over
  hand-rolling — it knows the conventions in this file (locators, `@UseCase`, naming, etc.).
- **Karibu is gone.** Any `com.github.mvysny.kaributesting.*` import is a mistake — the project is all
  `SpringBrowserlessTest` / `ComponentQuery` now. The `karibu-test` skill is obsolete.

## Test class naming — `UC<NNN><UseCaseName>Test`

Tests that verify a use case are named after the use case, **not** the view. Format:
`UC<NNN><UseCaseNameInPascalCase>Test`, e.g `UC001ViewWelcomePageTest`, `UC004FindOwnersByLastNameTest`,
`UC007AddPetToOwnerTest`. The `NNN` matches the `UC-NNN-*.md` file in `docs/use_cases/`.

If a view is touched by multiple use cases, write one `UC<NNN>…Test` class per use case rather than one `XxxViewTest`
covering all of them. Keep the test file in the **same package as the view under test** and name the class after the UC.

**Exception — cross-cutting tests.** `ArchitectureTest` (the ArchUnit rules behind
[`development.md`](development.md)) and `PetclinicApplicationTests` verify no single use case, so they sit in the
root package under their own names. Everything that *does* verify a use case follows the format above.

(never on the class — the annotation is `@Target(METHOD)` and cannot go on a class):

UC-002 is implemented. The full `./mvnw test` passes: 66 tests, 0 failures, including ArchUnit and the four traceability sensors. I didn't run `./mvnw verify`, so the Playwright layer and the merged coverage report haven't run.

**What I added**
- **`vet/domain/Vet.java` and `Specialty.java`**: plain `Serializable` records with no validation.
- **`vet/domain/VetRepository.java`**: a read-only repository with `findPage(offset, limit)` and `count()`. Each vet's specialties come back in the same query, sorted by name (BR-002), so there is one query per page rather than one per vet.
- **`vet/ui/VetsView.java`**: the page at `/vets`, inside `MainLayout`. It shows a grid with "First Name", "Last Name" and "Specialties". Rows load as you scroll (BR-001), a vet with no specialties shows "none", and no login is needed (BR-003).
- **`core/ui/MainLayout.java`**: the "Veterinarians" menu item now points at `VetsView.class` instead of the plain string `"vets"`.
- **`vet/ui/UC002ViewVeterinariansTest.java`**: tests for the main scenario, A1 (no vets gives an empty grid), BR-001, BR-002 and BR-003. The BR-001 test adds 120 extra vets and checks that the grid fetches them on demand and that the last one is reached correctly.

**Decisions and things left for you**
- **Vet order:** the spec only fixes the order of specialties, not of vets. I sorted vets by last name, then first name, then id. The id tie-break keeps pages from overlapping or skipping rows.
- **Status line:** I left UC-002 at `Approved`. CLAUDE.md says to run `aiup-vaadin-jooq:coverage-check` before changing a status, and that skill isn't available in this session (neither are the `.claude/` hooks). Moving UC-002 to `Implemented` or `Done` also means updating the status of FR-003, NFR-001–003 and C-010/011 in `docs/requirements.md` to match.
- **TC-006:** the end-to-end journey for this use case has no Playwright `TC006…IT` test yet, so it stays `Approved`.
- **Menu-link test:** clicking a menu item does nothing in browserless tests, because the browser handles that navigation. The test checks that the "Veterinarians" item's path is `vets` and goes there directly.
- **Database:** this environment has no Docker. The project's local-Postgres replacement (`vb-postgres`) handled code generation and the tests instead.

Nothing is committed.
